verdict.rationale: Anytype's own infrastructure does background syncing and backups automatically. Its docs state that not even Anytype can see your content, and the apps cover macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android. Hands-on users report that sync between devices works well. One community report says data is not encrypted at rest on the local disk, but that concerns local storage, not whether the vendor can read synced data. missing for 10: technical documentation of the end-to-end encryption scheme (key handling, what metadata the sync nodes can see), independent verification that the vendor cannot read synced data

support.subject: As a power-user, an official sync service keeps my notes updated across all my devices with end-to-end encryption the vendor can't read

citations.quote: Our infrastructure handles background syncing and backups automatically, so you retain full ownership of your data without compromising your sovereignty.
Only you can access your spaces and grant access to others — not even Anytype can see your content.
It is available on macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android.
You can work completely offline, sync across your own devices, or self-host your data.
It syncs notes between devices, works offline, is cross-platform
